scope: api/src event-emitting mechanisms, reservation lifecycle coverage, platform_events schema safety, tenant safety of event writes, doc-vs-code drift
method: source tracing (grep call sites, not just definitions), live schema inspection via psql against rezv-test-pg databases (rezervno_verify, rezervno_test2), live single-file test execution (npx tsx --test --test-force-exit), read-only. No api/src edits made. No full suite / build / migration run.

handoff_verification.quoted_claim: M0 event substrate - lib/events.ts emit() is a WEBHOOK dispatcher, not a log; of its 7 declared domain events exactly one is called; recordEvent() (the real platform_events writer) is called only from site-orders.ts. Zero reservation-lifecycle events are logged.

clauses.clause: emit() is a WEBHOOK dispatcher, not a log
clauses.evidence: api/src/lib/events.ts:35-67 - emit() queries db.webhook.findMany() for the restaurants active webhook subscriptions and enqueues one delivery job per hook (kind:webhook). It performs zero writes to any durable event-log table. Delivery itself happens later in api/src/lib/worker.ts:41 -> deliverWebhook() (api/src/lib/events.ts:122-159), which does an HTTP POST, not a DB insert.
clauses.verified_by: file read plus grep for db.* calls inside emit()

clauses.clause: of its 7 declared domain events exactly one is called
clauses.evidence: api/src/lib/events.ts:20-23 declares the DomainEvent union with 8 members, not 7: reservation.created, reservation.cancelled, reservation.completed, reservation.no_show, waitlist.joined, waitlist.seated, customer.vip_reached, coupon.redeemed. Grep for emit( across api/src found exactly one call site: api/src/lib/reservations.ts:420 (event: reservation.created). So the 1-of-N-called part is correct; N=8, not 7.
clauses.verified_by: Grep pattern for emit( across api/src; manual count of the union members

clauses.clause: recordEvent() (the real platform_events writer) is called only from site-orders.ts
clauses.evidence: True for the literal recordEvent() function: 4 call sites, all in api/src/lib/site-orders.ts (lines 206, 485, 597, 641), none related to reservations (they log site.order.created / site.trial.created / site.order.activated / site.order.rejected - the marketing/subscription funnel on the public landing site). But platform_events has a second writer, recordEventsDetailed(), defined in api/src/lib/platform-events.ts:134-146 and called from api/src/app/api/v1/telemetry/route.ts:276 - this is the actual client-facing, higher-traffic ingestion path used by customer/business/company analytics.js. The handoff names only recordEvent() and thereby omits the telemetry path entirely from the writer inventory.
clauses.verified_by: Grep for recordEvent(, recordEvents( and recordEventsDetailed( across api/src; read of telemetry/route.ts

clauses.evidence: True only if event is read narrowly as a row in platform_events. False in the load-bearing sense: every reservation status transition (hold expiry, confirmation, check-in/arrival, seating, no-show, completion, cancellation, QR check-in) is durably logged, append-only, with actor/reason/timestamp, in the reservation_events table via the single writer transitionReservation() at api/src/lib/lifecycle.ts:79-136 (tx.reservationEvent.create at lifecycle.ts:125). This table is not decorative: it is the real point-in-time feature source consumed by the working no-show ML model (api/src/lib/no-show-model.ts:432-509 and :776-806, both using a settled_at sub-query against reservation_events), by api/src/lib/fraud.ts:127-132, and by api/src/lib/waitlist.ts:79-84 (dining-duration estimation). A fresh session reading this sentence would reasonably conclude there is no reservation-lifecycle log at all; there is one, it is well engineered, and it is the actual substrate the one working ML model depends on.
clauses.verified_by: grep for transitionReservation( call sites (9 call sites across reservations.ts, lifecycle.ts crons, reservation-lifecycle-ops.ts, tables.ts, cancel/route.ts, restaurant/reservations/[code]/status/route.ts); grep for reservationEvent.create (exactly 1 call site, lifecycle.ts:125); grep for reservation_events consumers in no-show-model.ts, fraud.ts and waitlist.ts; live schema check against rezv-test-pg/rezervno_verify; live test execution: tests/temporal-leakage.integration.test.mts (3/3 pass, exit 0) and tests/feature-parity.integration.test.mts (4/4 pass, exit 0) against rezervno_test2, both exercising the reservation_events-backed history query

handoff_verification.overall_assessment: The handoffs individual factual atoms (webhook-only emit, 1-of-N called, recordEvent-only-in-site-orders) are each roughly right but the count is off by one and the writer inventory is incomplete. The real defect is the closing sentences framing: it collapses platform_events has no reservation rows (true) into reservation lifecycle is not logged (false), which erases the existence and importance of reservation_events. A fresher, more accurate, already-written analysis of this exact area exists at docs/ml/P0-audit.md (uncommitted, dated 2026-09-02) and independently reaches the same corrected conclusions this audit reaches (it even states the correct count of 8, not 7). That file never propagated into SESSION-HANDOFF.md's summary.

findings.claim: SESSION-HANDOFF.md:95-97 states Zero reservation-lifecycle events are logged, which will be read by every fresh session (it is the paste-ready onboarding prompt's referenced map) as there is no reservation lifecycle log, when in fact reservation_events (migration api/prisma/sql/004-lifecycle-events.sql) is a complete, append-only, point-in-time-safe log of every status transition, and is the actual feature source for the one working ML model in the codebase.
findings.verified_by: source trace of every transitionReservation() call site plus live schema check plus live test execution (temporal-leakage, feature-parity, both exit 0)

findings.claim: platform_events is schema-complete and well engineered (append-only, occurredAt vs ingestedAt separation, trust levels, per-trust-level retention) but is functionally a dead end today: (a) zero reservation-domain events are ever written to it; (b) of the 12 allowlisted type prefixes in the telemetry route, client code across apps/customer, apps/business, apps/company and shared/ only ever emits 2 constant type strings, app.opened and page.viewed, confirmed by grep with zero dynamic or templated type construction found anywhere; (c) no model, recommender, or feature builder in api/src reads platform_events at all - the only reader is an admin health-check aggregate added 2026-08-26 (api/src/app/api/v1/admin/telemetry/route.ts) whose own header comment states that before that date platform_events had zero readers in the entire codebase.
findings.evidence: api/src/app/api/v1/telemetry/route.ts:119-141 (allowlist); apps/customer/js/analytics.js:88, apps/customer/js/data/discover.js:16, apps/business/js/analytics.js:82, apps/business/js/routing.js:71, apps/company/js/analytics.js:82, apps/company/js/data.js:31, shared/js/analytics.panel.js:82 (the only 2 event type strings ever sent - app.opened, page.viewed); api/src/app/api/v1/admin/telemetry/route.ts:11-15 (comment documenting the zero-reader history); grep for db.platformEvent.findMany/groupBy/aggregate across api/src returned only this one file
findings.verified_by: grep across apps js and shared js for track( and rzTrack( call sites; grep across api/src for platformEvent read methods

findings.claim: Beyond the 7 dead DomainEvent members, audit.ts independently declares reservation.cancel as an AuditAction with zero call sites anywhere in api/src, and declares coupon.redeem which is spelled differently from events.ts's coupon.redeemed for what is nominally the same business event - the two vocabularies are not just partially unused, they are not even mutually consistent.

findings.claim: Reservation creation itself is never written to reservation_events, only post-creation status transitions are (transitionReservation() requires an existing row and a from-not-equal-to change). The Prisma schema comment describing fromStatus as null for the first event describes an intent the code never fulfills. Currently harmless because reservations.createdAt on the main row already carries the creation timestamp, and the no-show model's history sub-query falls back safely (undercounts, never overcounts) when no matching event exists, but reservation_events alone cannot answer when or by whom a reservation was created, only how it changed afterward.
findings.evidence: api/prisma/schema.prisma:588 (comment) versus api/src/lib/reservations.ts:502 (tx.reservation.create, no reservationEvent write) versus api/src/lib/lifecycle.ts:125 (the only reservationEvent.create call site, always has a non-null from-status because it requires an existing row)
findings.verified_by: grep for reservationEvent.create (1 call site) plus read of insertReservation()

findings.claim: POST /api/v1/telemetry accepts restaurantId from the client-supplied request body per event, not from auth context, and validates only that the id refers to some existing restaurant, not that the caller has any relationship to it. Any client, anonymous or authenticated, can tag a telemetry event, and thereby its derived tenantId, to any real restaurant. This differs from the reservation-creation path (restaurant_id from body, but staff callers are checked against their own branch, and the value is the actual booking target) and the site-orders path (tenantId is always server-generated, never client-supplied). Practical impact today is near zero because platform_events has no ML or feature consumer (see M0-004) and clients only ever send app.opened/page.viewed with no restaurant-scoped payload data, but the design pattern is exactly the body-sourced-tenant-id anti-pattern CLAUDE.md prohibits for restaurant-scoped writes, and it will become a real data-poisoning vector for the intelligence layer the day platform_events gains a real consumer.
findings.evidence: api/src/app/api/v1/telemetry/route.ts:188-192 (restaurant lookup keyed only on client-supplied ids, no ownership check), :251-252 (restaurantId/tenantId attached from that lookup)
findings.verified_by: read of telemetry/route.ts POST_impl end to end; not classified as blocker because no read or mutation of another tenant's private data occurs and there is currently no downstream consumer to poison; see decision package in the markdown report for the recommended fix before platform_events gains a consumer

findings.claim: schema.prisma:1638 and :1640, and api/src/lib/platform-events.ts:165, cite migration 046 and migration 047 for the trust_level index and the retention index on platform_events. The actual migrations are 059b-telemetry-trust-boundary.sql (trust_level_idx) and 060-platform-events-retention.sql (trust_ingested_idx); 046 and 047 are unrelated migrations (customer-insight-spend-nullable, menu-item-category). No functional impact, but misleads anyone tracing why an index exists.

findings.claim: The waitlist lifecycle (joined, offered, accepted, declined, expired or no_response, cancelled, seated) has no append-only event log at all, unlike the reservation lifecycle. WaitlistEntry rows are mutated in place; once an entry cycles through states, only the latest occurrence of offeredAt, respondedAt and seatedAt survives - prior states and their timestamps are overwritten, not preserved. This is a genuine, durable hole in the data foundation for anything modeling waitlist behavior such as offer-decline rate, time-to-seat, or repeat-offer patterns.
findings.evidence: api/src/lib/waitlist.ts:201 (create), :340,433,478,485,506,551,598 (in-place update or updateMany calls, no companion history-table writes); DomainEvent's waitlist.joined and waitlist.seated (events.ts:22) are declared but never called, consistent with M0-002/M0-003
findings.verified_by: grep for waitlistEntry.update/updateMany/create across waitlist.ts; grep for a WaitlistEvent model in schema.prisma - none exists

platform_events.evidence: grep for db.platformEvent.update/delete/upsert across api/src: zero matches. Only .create (platform-events.ts:106) and .createMany (platform-events.ts:140) exist, both insert-only with skipDuplicates. prunePlatformEvents() (platform-events.ts:201-223) does DELETE rows past retention, a documented, deliberate exception for retention, not mutation, gated by trust_level plus ingested_at.
platform_events.evidence_2: schema.prisma:1611 occurredAt (event time, client-influenced, clamped to a bounded window by clampOccurredAt in platform-events.ts:70-77) versus :1612 ingestedAt and :1633 serverReceivedAt (both server-authoritative, default now())
platform_events.monotonic_ordering_key: partial - id is a random uuid, not sortable, but occurredAt, ingestedAt and serverReceivedAt give usable temporal ordering; no bigserial sequence column exists
platform_events.live_schema_evidence: psql against rezervno_verify (the meta-command that lists a table's columns and indexes) matches schema.prisma:1608-1643 column for column and index for index; no drift found for this table

reservation_events.evidence: grep for tx.reservationEvent.create/update/delete/upsert across api/src: exactly one call site total (lifecycle.ts:125), it is a create, and transitionReservation() is documented and grep-verified as the only function that writes reservation status at all
reservation_events.event_time_vs_ingest_time: n/a - createdAt is set server-side at the exact moment of the real transition, inside the same DB transaction as the status change, so there is no client-supplied event time to diverge from ingest time here
reservation_events.cascade_delete_risk: reservation_events has ON DELETE CASCADE from reservations(id). No db.reservation.delete or deleteMany call site exists anywhere in api/src (grep confirmed), so this is currently inert, but it means a future GDPR/right-to-erasure feature that hard-deletes a reservation would silently destroy its lifecycle history too - worth a note for whoever builds that feature.
reservation_events.live_schema_evidence: psql against rezervno_verify matches schema.prisma:584-596 column for column and index for index; no drift found for this table
